problem: New, from the step3-jobs-fix-3-C1-1/C1-2 fix pass (the C1-2 part). The running branch now treats a record as a start in flight when _pid_alive(record['pid']) is False, but that pid is only the product's group leader. The product lock is inherited by the whole group, and stop_products signals the group (killpg). So a product whose leader died while other members of its group live on, still holding the lock, is now taken for a start in flight. Every env start then waits _STARTING_WAIT (5 s) for a running record that never comes and fails with 'another start of this subject is still settling', at the same commit and at another commit, until env stop or the checkpoint clears it. Before the fix, the same commit answered the record and another commit replaced the product (D14). Probe in a scratch copy, with run = 'sleep 60 & wait' (the leader is sh, sleep keeps the lock) and the leader killed with SIGKILL. Fixed code: the second and third starts each returned 1 'still settling' after 5.1 s, at the same commit and at another. Pre-fix mutant: the same commit answered at once, and another commit stopped the group and started a new product (new pid, exit 0). A second, smaller effect: _wait_for_running never probes the lock again. When the holder dies without writing a record (a start call killed between taking the lock and writing 'starting'), the waiting call still waits the full 5 s and errors although the lock came free after 0.7 s. At another commit the pre-fix code took the lock and started. The new tests do not cover either case: they use the dead pid 999999 under a holder process, whose group does not exist.
proposed_resolution: Judge the product by its group, as stop_products does: treat the record as live while os.killpg(pid, 0) succeeds (ProcessLookupError means gone, PermissionError means live). That is a group-liveness helper beside _pid_alive, used in _held_answer's running branch and in _wait_for_running. Only a record whose group is gone, under a held lock, is a start in flight. In _wait_for_running, probe the product lock on each poll and return None when it is free, so the caller takes the lock and starts. Add tests in test_env.py: (a) run 'sleep 30 & wait', SIGKILL the leader, then a start at the same commit answers at once with exit 0, and a start at another commit stops the surviving group and starts a new product; (b) a stale running record under a holder that exits after about 0.5 s without writing, where the start returns 0 well inside _STARTING_WAIT. Keep the four C1-2 tests passing. Update the env-start.md sentence ('a record whose product is gone') to say the product's process group.
